args.content_digest: MARK 2 CRISPCRUST classified as descriptive on the Abercrombie spectrum. The mark is a real-word combination (crisp + crust) that directly states the frozen pizza line's defining feature — its notably crisp crust — as confirmed by the test kitchen and recited in the client letter. Per the firm rule memo, the dividing line between descriptive and suggestive turns on whether the mark states the attribute directly (descriptive) or requires consumer imagination/multi-step inference (suggestive). The letter recites that a consumer reading the mark on the freezer door understands immediately, without imagination or inference, that the pizza has a crisp crust. Accordingly, no mental leap is required, placing CRISPCRUST squarely in the descriptive category.
